introduction: GeorgiaLegalAid directs residents to civil legal help according to their county. Tell the intake provider immediately if you have an eviction notice, court response deadline or hearing.
description: GeorgiaLegalAid directs residents to civil legal help according to their county. Tell the intake provider immediately if you have an eviction notice, court response deadline o

sections.who: The legal-aid provider reviews eligibility, case type and available capacity. The website is an information and referral route; it does not automatically assign a lawyer.
sections.get: Residents can find legal information and contact the organization serving their area. Representation depends on the provider’s assessment.
sections.docs:

sections.apply:
1. Use the county pathway

    For Fulton, Clayton, Cobb, Gwinnett or DeKalb, the directory points to Atlanta Legal Aid. Other Georgia counties are directed to Georgia Legal Services Program.

  2. Request intake

    Use the Find Legal Help page for the appropriate online application or phone contact.

  3. Confirm the next step

    Ask whether your case has been accepted and what you must do about any deadline while the request is pending.
sections.after: Keep copies of the intake and provider response. Continue tracking court dates unless the provider gives specific instructions for your case.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using GeorgiaLegalAid county intake directory. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Atlanta Legal Aid serves the five counties identified above; the directory directs other counties to Georgia Legal Services Program.
Is there a service for older residents?
The directory lists the Georgia Senior Legal Hotline at 888-257-9519 for people aged 60 or older.
Will submitting a request stop an eviction case?
Do not assume so. Ask the provider about your court papers and deadlines.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
